issues.body: `_NON_PLAIN_START` still treats every value beginning with `&` or `!` as a complete non-plain node. YAML anchors and tags are properties that can prefix a scalar, so `name: &label Publish for issue #1135` and `name: !custom Publish for issue #1135` can still contain a truncated plain scalar while `_plain_name_value()` returns `None`. No new self-test covers these cases.
issues.fix_hint: Lexically consume anchor/tag properties, then classify and scan the following node. Keep aliases separate because an alias is itself a complete node. Add failing fixtures for anchored and tagged plain names containing ` #1234`, plus safe quoted or otherwise non-plain property-prefixed cases.
issues.title: Anchored and tagged plain scalars still bypass the gate

issues.body: `_multiline_truncation_offence()` still returns immediately on a blank line, even though its docstring acknowledges that YAML can fold such a line into a continuing plain scalar. A sufficiently indented continuation containing ` #1135` after that blank line can therefore evade the gate. The self-tests still do not exercise this valid continuation shape.
issues.fix_hint: Handle blank lines according to YAML plain-scalar continuation rules instead of terminating unconditionally. Add a regression fixture in which a valid multiline plain `name:` resumes after a blank line and contains a whitespace-prefixed issue reference, together with a safe paragraph-style multiline fixture.
issues.title: Blank lines still bypass multiline scalar detection

verdict.summary: Round 3 is stagnant: both round-2 major false-negative classes remain unchanged. Anchor/tag-prefixed scalar nodes are still excluded wholesale by `_NON_PLAIN_START`, and multiline scanning still terminates at the first blank line despite acknowledging that YAML may continue the scalar afterward. The self-test suite adds no fixtures for either case, so the gate still does not fulfill its stated promise to flag every affected plain `name:`/`run-name:` scalar.
